user_query: Under which conditions does LINE(1st) beat LINE(2nd) on semantic and syntactic analogy, given that first-order proximity is the stronger setting here?
llm_response: LINE(1st) beats LINE(2nd) when the graph setting is dominated by first-order proximity, i.e., when preserving direct edge relationships is more important than preserving neighborhood similarity. In that stronger first-order-proximity regime, LINE(1st) performs better on both semantic and syntactic analogy tasks than LINE(2nd).
llm_confidence_reasoning: This is a high-level summary of the reported comparison, but the exact experimental conditions and dataset details are not fully specified in the question, so there is some uncertainty.
